title: TriNet Unveils 2027 State of the Workplace Report
summary: TriNet, a leading provider of comprehensive human resources solutions for small and medium-size businesses (SMBs) today unveiled its 2027 State of the Workplace report, an annual look at employer and employee sentiment across the SMB landscape throughout the nation.
body_markdown:
### *Survey of 1,000+ SMB respondents finds rising satisfaction and engagement amid increased AI use and in-office work*


###### ****


**Dublin, CA — November 18, 2026 —**[TriNet](https://www.trinet.com/) (NYSE: TNET), a leading provider of comprehensive human resources solutions for small and medium-size businesses (SMBs) today unveiled its[2027 State of the Workplace](https://www.trinet.com/resources/research/state-of-work?utm_source=general&utm_medium=press-release&utm_campaign=stateofworkq426&asset_id=A102226SW6) report, an annual look at employer and employee sentiment across the SMB landscape throughout the nation.


Based on a survey of more than 1,000 SMB respondents, including 575 full-time employees and 525 employers, the report examines some of the most pressing workplace issues facing SMBs, including employee engagement and satisfaction, return-to-office trends, benefits and AI in the workplace.


Conducted by TriNet and administered by Qualtrics, the study also examines year-over-year shifts and differences across generations, offering a snapshot of how the SMB workplace continues to evolve.


“As businesses navigate an increasingly complex world of work, leaders have an opportunity to be intentional about the kind of workplace they want to create. That starts with listening to employees, understanding their evolving needs and recognizing that the employee experience plays an important role in business success,” said Catherine Wragg, Chief People Officer, TriNet. “The findings in this report offer valuable perspective for leaders looking to make informed decisions, strengthen their organizations and create an environment where both their people and their businesses can thrive.”


Key findings from the report include:


- **Time in-office and employee satisfaction increase:** 73% of employers report working in-office four or more days a week, up from 58% the previous year. The share of employers reporting three days as their preferred in-office cadence declined from 26% to 17%. At the same time, workplace satisfaction reached a three-year high, with 93% of employers and 86% of employees reporting some level of satisfaction.
- **Employee engagement hits a three-year high** : 55% of employees surveyed say they are extremely engaged in their jobs, the highest level reported in three years. Confidence also rebounded, with 58% saying they have the knowledge and skills needed to succeed in their roles, up from 49% last year.
- **Benefits are the most important but the least understood** : At 79%, benefits are the biggest consideration for employees when looking for a job.Medical insurance is the most important among individual benefits at 81%. However, there is a gap in understanding of benefits offerings, with 80% of employers believing their people understand the benefits they offer, while just 65% of employees say they are clear on their options.
- **AI is now routine, but a guidance gap remains:** 90% of employers say they have provided employees with guidance on using AI at work, but only 66% of employees say they have received it. AI usage remains at a three-year high, with 75% of employers and 51% of employees reporting at least moderate use. 18% of employees say they never use AI at work.


The full 2027 ****[State of the Workplace Report](https://www.trinet.com/resources/research/state-of-work?utm_source=general&utm_medium=press-release&utm_campaign=stateofworkq426&asset_id=A102226SW6) is available now.
